_comment: Source of truth for how Bristlenose spells platform, hardware, distro and tool names in prose. scripts/check-docs-terms.py reads 'forbidden' (case-sensitive regexes, matched in prose only, never code); tests/test_check_docs_terms.py pins every 'canonical' to the table in docs/glossary.md. A row with no forbidden patterns is documentation only.

terms.evidence: arm.com trademark list ('Trademark list - Arm®', 'Arm-based systems'); Microsoft Learn writes 'Windows on Arm'. Rebrand from ARM was 2017.
apple.com and support.apple.com write 'Apple silicon' (lowercase s) in running text.
Renamed from Raspbian in 2020 (from memory, not re-fetched; the raspberrypi.com software page did not return text to a plain fetch).
opensuse.org writes openSUSE, lowercase o, including at the start of a sentence.
elementary.io writes elementary OS, lowercase e.

keep_in_code: redhat (a path, repo or package name)
terms.evidence: redhat.com prose writes Red Hat; 'redhat' appears only in URLs and identifiers.
ffmpeg.org writes FFmpeg in prose. The command and the Fedora package name stay lowercase in code.

keep_in_code: pypi (a URL or package index name)

terms.evidence: snapcraft.io writes Snap Store. House style: 'the Snap' for our package, `snap` only as the command.
Usage rule, not a spelling: x64 in Windows prose (Microsoft's word), x86_64 in Linux prose, amd64 only where Debian or the Snap itself uses it. For a lay reader, '64-bit Intel and AMD'.
Microsoft Learn mixes 'WinGet' and 'winget' (counted 54 and 12 on the winget overview page, 20 Nov 2026), so neither is banned. Our docs write winget, matching the command.
Fedora's build service; capital C in prose. Not machine-checked.
